descriptor: River clean-up charity and annual impact report

voice.summary: Speaks like a volunteer coordinator reporting back to the people who funded the work: plain numbers first, gratitude second, no drama. Every claim is tied to a stretch of river, a month or a pair of hands.
dos: Lead with the number, then say what it meant for the river
Name the people, places and months behind each figure
Admit when a goal is behind pace and say what happens next
donts: Do not use disaster language or guilt to raise money
Do not round up a result to make it sound bigger
Do not use charity jargon like stakeholders or capacity building

taglines: A cleaner river, stretch by stretch
Every bag counts. We counted them.
Volunteers in, litter out, river better
Healthy water starts with ordinary Saturdays
boilerplate: Tidewater Trust is a river charity that organises volunteer clean-ups, tracks every kilogram of litter removed and publishes an open annual report on where its funding and effort go.

logo.note: A simple wave line suits a river charity whose whole job is keeping moving water clean.
